title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous and next pages. M_{ρ,σ} is an algebraic group. It has neutral components, characters to G_m and μ2×μ2, and tori T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ. It is written as a semi-direct product M_{ρ,σ} = M_{ρ,σ}(0)·SG (32). Here SG embeds via j as the normal subgroup 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ}, with quotient T_{ρ,σ} ≅ M_{ρ,σ}(0) (34–36). Earlier, an abstract group M_{ρ,σ}[0] was defined as a semi-direct product M_{ρ,σ}(0)·L_0, with L_0 ⊂ SG. A canonical embedding i: M[0] → M was given (37–38), extending the identity on M(0) and equal to j on L_0.

This page restates that construction intrinsically:
- The conjugation action of M(0) on SG ≅ 𝔊^+ normalizes j(L_0), now identified with L_0.
- Hence the product M(0)·L_0 is a subgroup of M_{ρ,σ}, canonically isomorphic to M[0] through its semi-direct product description.

Remark: one has M[0] ⊂ Norm_{M_{ρ,σ}}(L_0). The reverse inclusion fails. Since M = M(0)⋉𝔊^+ and M(0) ⊂ Norm(L_0), we get Norm_M(L_0) = M(0)·Norm_{𝔊^+}(L_0). So equality would amount to L_0 being self-normalizing in SG ≅ 𝔊^+, which 'is not true at all'.

Grothendieck contrasts this with the profinite situation. In \hat𝔊_{0,3}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞} (free profinite on two generators), the closed subgroup generated by the loop ε_0 is self-normalizing. The same holds for the subgroups generated by the other basic loops. He adds parenthetically that he learned this fact from someone else (name or wording illegible).

Purpose: to identify the stabilizer subgroup M[0] (the subgroup 'at the base point 0') inside the big group M_{ρ,σ}, which acts in his study of the 'loop equation' (Teichmüller/GT-type symmetries of P^1 minus 3 points). He records that the profinite self-normalizing property of inertia does not pass to this linear-algebraic envelope.
errors: The page states only the inclusion M[0] ⊂ Norm(L_0), and correctly notes that the reverse fails. No claim of equality is made: the word 'Proposition' was crossed out and replaced by 'Remarque', apparently for this reason.
Equation labels are inconsistent with neighbouring pages: '(49)' appears where (32)–(38) were just used. This is likely a misreading or an earlier numbering; not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Semi-direct product subgroup M(0)·L_0 inside M = M(0)⋉SG, because M(0) normalizes L_0, identified with the abstractly defined M[0]
Norm_M(L_0) = M(0)·Norm_{SG}(L_0); equality with M(0)·L_0 iff L_0 is self-normalizing in SG
In the free profinite group \hat π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}), the procyclic inertia subgroup generated by a loop ε_i is self-normalizing (indeed its own normalizer)
ideas.modern_name: self-normalizing / commensurably terminal cusp inertia subgroups in profinite surface groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes (centralizers in free profinite products, mid-1980s); H. Nakamura (Galois rigidity of pro-π_1 of punctured lines, ~1990); widely used in anabelian geometry (Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche discussions of inertia subgroups; unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly notes that the self-normalizing property of inertia subgroups holds in the profinite \hat𝔊_{0,3} but fails in the algebraic-group version he is studying. He says he learned the profinite fact second-hand. This documents his awareness of the property, but it is a known result, not a new one.
missed.quote: bien que le fait analogue soit vrai dans le groupe profini \hat𝔊_{0,3}, pour le sous-groupe engendré par ε_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild historical interest: it shows that inertia self-normalization, a key ingredient later in Nakamura's and Mochizuki's anabelian rigidity results, was on Grothendieck's radar in the Longue Marche period.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine group-theoretic bookkeeping (a semi-direct product subgroup and its normalizer). It also contains a passing mention of a known profinite fact, self-normalizing inertia, which Grothendieck says he learned from others.
transcription_corrections: M_{φ,σ} should read M_{ρ,σ} throughout; '(o)' and '[o]' are (0) and [0].
'\hat G^{+}_{ρ,σ}' should be the fraktur group 𝔊^{+}_{ρ,σ} (no hat). Only the profinite group \hat𝔊_{0,3} carries a hat.
The crossed-out heading above 'Remarque' is 'Proposition', and the crossed-out label next to the formula is an equation number.

The final lines are partly illegible. They seem to say that the analogous fact also holds for the subgroups generated by the other loops (ε_1, ε_∞), followed by a parenthetical 'que je n'ai appris que par ...' naming a source or 'ouï-dire'; the reading 'par fait' is doubtful.
